verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。）我所赞美的　神啊，求你不要闭口不言。
verses.en: For the music director, a psalm of David.O God whom I praise, do not ignore me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 109. Appealing to God’s justice, the psalmist asks God to vindicate him and to bring severe judgment down upon his enemies.
verses.commentary:
109:1 "O God of my praise" This phrase is found only here and in Deut. 10:21, but the concept is recurrent
(i.e., Psalm 146-148). The LXX translates this phrase as "O God do not pass over my praise in silence."

The title/name, "God," is Eloah, which is the SINGULAR for of Elohim.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "Do not be silent" This is a Hebrew idiom for YHWH to hear and respond to the prayer of
a faithful follower (cf. Ps. 28:1; 35:22; 38:12; 83:1). The VERB (BDB 361 II, KB 357, Qal
IMPERFECT) is used in a JUSSIVE sense.

verses.zh: 因为恶人的嘴和诡诈人的口已经张开攻击我；他们用撒谎的舌头对我说话。
verses.en: For they say cruel and deceptive things to me;they lie to me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “do not be deaf.”
verses.commentary:
109:2-3 There is power in words both for blessing and for hurting. Our words reveal our hearts! See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SPEECH.

The AB (p. 100) sees these verses as imagery from vocabulary of animal attacks.

- mouth of attacking animals (cf. Ps. 22:13; Lam. 3:46-47)

- "speaking" (BDB 180) in sense of "pursuing"

- "surrounding" like a pack of animals

verses.zh: 他们围绕我，说怨恨的话，又无故地攻打我。
verses.en: They surround me and say hateful things;[NOTE:1] they attack me for no reason.
notes: Heb “for a mouth of evil and a mouth of deceit against me they open, they speak with me [with] a tongue of falsehood.”

verses.zh: 他们与我为敌以报我爱，但我专心祈祷。
verses.en: They repay my love with accusations,[NOTE:1] but I continue to pray.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and [with] words of hatred they surround me.”
Heb “in place of my love they oppose me.”
verses.commentary:
109:4-5 Being attacked is painful but being attacked by those you trusted and befriended is doubly painful
(cf. Ps. 35:12; 38:20).

109:4b

NASB
"But I am in prayer"

NKJV
"But I myself to prayer"

"even while I make prayer for them"

The MT's meaning is uncertain, as you can tell from the variety of English
translations. Literally, the Hebrew is "and I a prayer."

109:5a "they have repaid me evil for good" We live in a fallen and unfair world. This is
not the world God intended it to be! The psalmist's sense of his friends'/family's hatred surprised
him (cf. Ps. 35:12; 38:20; Jer. 18:20). This was also Jesus' experience!

verses.zh: 他们向我以恶报善，以恨报爱。
verses.en: They repay me evil for good[NOTE:1] and hate for love.
notes: Heb “and I, prayer.”

verses.zh: 愿你派一个恶人辖制他，派一个对头站在他右边！
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Appoint an evil man to testify against him.[NOTE:2] May an accuser stand[NOTE:3] at his right side.
notes: Heb “and they set upon me evil in place of good.”

In vv. 6-19 the psalmist calls on God to judge his enemies severely. Some attribute this curse-list to the psalmist’s enemies rather than the psalmist. In this case one should paraphrase v. 6: “They say about me, ‘Appoint an evil man, etc.’” Those supporting this line of interpretation point out that vv. 2-5 and 20 refer to the enemies’ attack on the psalmist being a verbal one. Furthermore in vv. 1-5, 20 the psalmist speaks of his enemies in the plural, while vv. 6-19 refer to an individual. This use of the singular in vv. 6-19 could be readily explained if this is the psalmist’s enemies’ curse on him. However, it is much more natural to understand vv. 6-19 as the psalmist’s prayer against his enemies. There is no introductory quotation formula in v. 6 to indicate that the psalmist is quoting anyone, and the statement “may the Lord repay my accusers in this way” in v. 20 most naturally appears to be a fitting conclusion to the prayer in vv. 6-19. But what about the use of the singular in vv. 6-19? Often in the psalms the psalmist will describe his enemies as a group, but then speak of them as an individual as well, as if viewing his adversaries collectively as one powerful foe. See, for example, Ps 7, where the psalmist uses both the plural (vv. 1, 6) and the singular (vv. 2, 4-5) in referring to enemies. Perhaps by using the singular in such cases, the psalmist wants to single out each enemy for individual attention, or perhaps he has one especially hostile enemy in mind who epitomizes the opposition of the whole group. This may well be the case in Ps 109. Perhaps we should understand the singular throughout vv. 6-19 in the sense of “each and every one.” For a lengthy and well-reasoned defense of the opposite view—that vv. 6-19 are a quotation of what the enemies said about the psalmist—see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 72-73.
Heb “appoint against him an evil [man].”
verses.commentary:
109:6-20 These two strophes sound so harsh to modern people. The psalmist is simply asking for the
covenant curses (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-30) on faithless Israelites to become a reality to his enemies. He
feels he is on YHWH's side; to attack him is to attack YHWH.

The Jewish Study Bible (p. 1407) says this is the longest cursing section in the Psalter. It is so
vivid and graphic that some commentators think it reflects what the enemies were saying against the psalmist
(i.e., Jerome Bible commentary, NJB, and NIV footnote). However, this cannot be proven from the MT. The only
evidence would be the SINGULAR form used in Ps. 109:6-19, which is probably a collective
SINGULAR.

109:6 "an accuser" This is the Hebrew term (BDB 966, cf. Ps. 109:20,29) that came to be a title for personified
evil, Satan.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATAN

verses.zh: 他受审判的时候，愿他出来担当罪名！愿他的祈祷反成为罪！
verses.en: When he is judged, he will be found[NOTE:1] guilty.[NOTE:2] Then his prayer will be regarded as sinful.
notes: The prefixed verbal form is taken as a jussive here (note the imperative in the preceding line).
The prefixed verbal form could be taken as a jussive, but the use of the imperfect form in the following line suggests that v. 7 anticipates the outcome of the accusation envisioned in v. 6.

verses.zh: 愿他的年日短少！愿别人得他的职分！
verses.en: May his days be few.[NOTE:1] May another take his job.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he will go out [as] a criminal” (that is, guilty).
The prefixed verbal forms (except those with vav [ו] consecutive) in vv. 8-20 are taken as jussives of prayer. Note the distinct jussive forms used in vv. 12-13, 15, 19.
verses.commentary:
109:8 "office" It is uncertain from the context what this word (BDB 824) means. It can refer to "stored provisions,"
cf. Isa. 15:7. The attacker had a place of prominence and power. This phrase (along with Ps. 69:25 from the LXX) is used in
Acts 1:20 as referring to Judas Iscariot. Acts used the word "office" as relating to an election for Judas' replacement as an Apostle.

verses.zh: 愿他的儿女为孤儿，他的妻子为寡妇！
verses.en: May his children[NOTE:1] be fatherless,and his wife a widow.
notes: The Hebrew noun פְּקֻדָּה (pequddah) can mean “charge” or “office,” though BDB 824 s.v. suggests that here it refers to his possessions.

verses.zh: 愿他的儿女漂流讨饭，从他们荒凉之处出来求食！
verses.en: May his children[NOTE:1] roam around begging,asking for handouts as they leave their ruined home.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “sons.”
Or “sons.”

verses.zh: 愿强暴的债主牢笼他一切所有的！愿外人抢他劳碌得来的！
verses.en: May the creditor seize[NOTE:1] all he owns.May strangers loot his property.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and roaming, may his children roam and beg, and seek from their ruins.” Some, following the LXX, emend the term וְדָרְשׁוּ (vedareshu, “and seek”) to יְגֹרְשׁוּ (yegoreshu; a Pual jussive, “may they be driven away” [see Job 30:5; cf. NIV, NRSV]), but דָּרַשׁ (darash) nicely parallels שִׁאֵלוּ (shiʾelu, “and beg”) in the preceding line.
Heb “lay snares for” (see Ps 38:12).

verses.zh: 愿无人向他延绵施恩！愿无人可怜他的孤儿！
verses.en: May no one show him kindness.[NOTE:1] May no one have compassion[NOTE:2] on his fatherless children.
notes: Heb “the product of his labor.”
Heb “may there not be for him one who extends loyal love.”

verses.zh: 愿他的后人断绝，名字被涂抹，不传于下代！
verses.en: May his descendants[NOTE:1] be cut off.[NOTE:2] May the memory of them be wiped out by the time the next generation arrives.[NOTE:3]
notes: Perhaps this refers to being generous (see Ps 37:21).
Or “offspring.”
On the expression cut off see Ps 37:28.

verses.zh: 愿他祖宗的罪孽被耶和华记念！愿他母亲的罪过不被涂抹！
verses.en: May his ancestors’[NOTE:1] sins be remembered by the Lord.May his mother’s sin not be forgotten.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in another generation may their name be wiped out.”
Or “fathers’ sins.”
verses.commentary:
109:14-15 This may be an allusion to the two books (i.e., the book of deeds and the book of life) which
symbolize God's memory.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

109:14 This verse reflects the words of Exod. 20:5 and Deut. 5:9-10 (also note Jer. 32:18). The
lifestyle and priorities of parents often affect the children.

verses.zh: 愿这些罪常在耶和华面前，使他的名号断绝于世！
verses.en: May the Lord be constantly aware of them[NOTE:1] and cut off the memory of his children[NOTE:2] from the earth.
notes: Heb “not be wiped out.”sn According to ancient Israelite theology and its doctrine of corporate solidarity and responsibility, children could be and often were punished for the sins of their parents. For a discussion of this issue see J. Kaminsky, Corporate Responsibility in the Hebrew Bible (JSOTSup). (Kaminsky, however, does not deal with Ps 109.)
Heb “may they [that is, the sins mentioned in v. 14] be before the Lord continually.”

verses.zh: 因为他不想施恩，却逼迫困苦穷乏的和伤心的人，要把他们治死。
verses.en: For he never bothered to show kindness;[NOTE:1] he harassed the oppressed and needyand killed the disheartened.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “their memory.” The plural pronominal suffix probably refers back to the children mentioned in v. 13, and for clarity this has been specified in the translation.
Heb “he did not remember to do loyal love.”

verses.zh: 他爱咒骂，咒骂就临到他；他不喜爱福乐，福乐就与他远离！
verses.en: He loved to curse[NOTE:1] others, so those curses have come upon him.[NOTE:2] He had no desire to bless anyone, so he has experienced no blessings.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and he chased an oppressed and needy man, and one timid of heart to put [him] to death.”

A curse in OT times consists of a formal appeal to God to bring judgment down upon another. Curses were sometimes justified (such as the one spoken by the psalmist here in vv. 6-19), but when they were not, the one pronouncing the curse was in danger of bringing the anticipated judgment down upon himself.

Heb “and he loved a curse and it came [upon] him.” A reference to the evil man experiencing a curse seems premature here, for the psalmist is asking God to bring judgment on his enemies. For this reason some (cf. NIV, NRSV) prefer to repoint the vav (ו) on “it came” as conjunctive and translate the verb as a jussive of prayer (“may it come upon him!”). The prefixed form with vav consecutive in the next line is emended in the same way and translated, “may it be far from him.” However, the psalmist may be indicating that the evil man’s lifestyle has already begun to yield its destructive fruit.
verses.commentary:
109:17-19 The curses referred to prayers for God to punish. The psalmist is asking for his persecutor's prayer
for vengeance to be turned back on themselves. In the OT if one is found to be a false witness in court, he bears the
punishment of the one falsely accused.

verses.zh: 他拿咒骂当衣服穿上；这咒骂就如水进他里面，像油入他的骨头。
verses.en: He made cursing a way of life,[NOTE:1] so curses poured into his stomach like waterand seeped into his bones like oil.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he did not delight in a blessing and it is far from him.”
Heb “he put on a curse as [if it were] his garment.”

verses.zh: 愿这咒骂当他遮身的衣服，当他常束的腰带！
verses.en: May a curse attach itself to him, like a garment one puts on,[NOTE:1] or a belt[NOTE:2] one wears continually.
notes: Heb “and it came like water into his inner being, and like oil into his bones.” This may refer to this individual’s appetite for cursing. For him cursing was as refreshing as drinking water or massaging oneself with oil. Another option is that the destructive effects of a curse are in view. In this case a destructive curse invades his very being, like water or oil. Some who interpret the verse this way prefer to repoint the verb from the preterite form וַתָּבֹא (vattavoʾ, “and it came”) to a jussive form וְתָבֹא (vetavoʾ, “and may it come!”).
Heb “may it be for him like a garment one puts on.”

verses.zh: 这就是我对头和用恶言议论我的人从耶和华那里所受的报应。
verses.en: May the Lord repay my accusers in this way,[NOTE:1] those who say evil things about[NOTE:2] me.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew noun מֵזַח (mezakh, “belt; waistband”) occurs only here in the OT. The form apparently occurs in Isa 23:10 as well, but an emendation is necessary there.
Heb “[may] this [be] the repayment to my accusers from the Lord.”
Or “against.”
verses.commentary:
109:20 This is a summary conclusion to Ps. 109:6-19. It could go with

- 109:6-19 (i.e., NASB, NKJV)

- the next strophe (cf. NRSV, TEV, NJB)

verses.zh: 主―耶和华啊，求你为你的名恩待我；因你的慈爱美好，求你搭救我！
verses.en: O Sovereign Lord,intervene on my behalf for the sake of your reputation.[NOTE:1] Because your loyal love is good, deliver me.
notes: The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “being; soul”) with a pronominal suffix is often equivalent to a pronoun, especially in poetry (see BDB 660 s.v. נֶפֶשׁ 4.a).
verses.commentary:
109:21-25 See full note at Contextual Insights, D.

109:21 "O God, the Lord" Literally this is YHWH Adoni.

of these combinations do not carry specific meaning but are poetic variety.

the person.

verses.zh: 因为我困苦穷乏，内心受伤。
verses.en: For I am oppressed and needy,and my heart beats violently within me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “but you, Lord, Master, deal with me for the sake of your name” or “on account of your name.” Here “name” stands metonymically for God’s reputation. The Psalmist’s appeal is for God to act consistently with, and therefore maintain, his reputation (as a deliverer of the righteous and one who punishes evildoers). Note that “for your name’s sake” is paralleled by “because your loyal love is good.” The point is that the Psalmist is making an appeal not based on his own personal whim or vendetta but is calling for judicial penalties (or the fulfillment of prior prophetic indictment).

verses.zh: 我如日影渐渐偏斜而去；我如蝗虫被抖出来。
verses.en: I am fading away like a shadow at the end of the day;[NOTE:1] I am shaken off like a locust.
notes: The verb in the Hebrew text (חָלַל, khalal) appears to be a Qal form from the root חלל meaning “pierced; wounded.” However, the Qal of this root is otherwise unattested. The translation assumes an emendation to יָחִיל (yakhil), a Qal imperfect from חוּל (khul, “tremble”) or to חֹלַל (kholal), a Polal perfect from חוּל (khul). See Ps 55:4, which reads לִבִּי יָחִיל בְּקִרְבִּי (libbi yakhil beqirbbi, “my heart trembles [i.e., “beats violently”] within me”).

verses.zh: 我因禁食，膝骨软弱；我身上的肉也渐渐瘦了。
verses.en: I am so starved my knees shake;[NOTE:1] I have turned into skin and bones.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “like a shadow when it is extended I go.” He is like a late afternoon shadow made by the descending sun that will soon be swallowed up by complete darkness. See Ps 102:11.
Heb “my knees stagger from fasting.”
verses.commentary:
109:24 This verse can be interpreted in two ways (see UBS Handbook, p. 944).

- the psalmist has been voluntarily fasting

- the psalmist has had no

- good food

- olive oil for anointing

verses.zh: 我受他们的羞辱，他们看见我便摇头。
verses.en: I am disdained by them.[NOTE:1] When they see me, they shake their heads.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and my flesh is lean away from fatness [i.e., “lean so as not to be fat”].”
Heb “as for me, I am a reproach to them.”
verses.commentary:
109:25 "they wag their head" This was a physical gesture of contempt (cf. 2 Kgs. 19:21; Job 16:4; Ps. 22:7; Isa. 37:22;
Jer. 18:16; 48:27; Lam. 2:15; Matt. 27:39; Mark 15:29).

verses.zh: 耶和华―我的　神啊，求你帮助我，照你的慈爱拯救我，
verses.en: Help me, O Lord my God.Because you are faithful to me, deliver me.[NOTE:1]
notes: They shake their heads. Apparently shaking the head was a taunting gesture. See also Job 16:4; Ps 22:7; Lam 2:15.
verses.commentary:
109:26-29 This is a typical OT role reversal motif. The psalmist wants to be vindicated by YHWH in the presence of
his enemies (cf. Ps. 23:5). This reflects a court scene.

verses.zh: 使他们知道这是你的手，是你―耶和华所行的事。
verses.en: Then they will realize[NOTE:1] this is your work[NOTE:2] and that you, Lord, have accomplished it.
notes: Heb “deliver me according to your faithfulness.”
After the preceding imperative, the prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose or result.

verses.zh: 任凭他们咒骂，惟愿你赐福；他们几时起来就必蒙羞，你的仆人却要欢喜。
verses.en: They curse, but you will bless.[NOTE:1] When they attack, they will be humiliated,[NOTE:2] but your servant will rejoice.
notes: Heb “that your hand [is] this.”
Another option is to translate the imperfect as a prayer/request (“may you bless”).
verses.commentary:
109:28 "Your servant" The NOUN "servant" (BDB 713) can be used of

- a slave

- subjects of a king

- worshipers (cf. Deut. 32:36,43)

- Levite singers (cf. Ps. 113:1; 134:1; 135:1)

- Israel (cf. Isa. 41:8-9)

- BDB 714, #6, suggests the usage here is simply a polite address to God (cf. Ps. 19:11,13; 27:9; 31:16; 35:27; 69:17; 143:2)

- NASB Study Bible (p. 856) sees it as a reference to the Davidic Messiah (cf. Ps. 78:20; Isa. 42:1)

- special title for leaders

- Abraham ‒ Gen. 26:24

- Isaac ‒ Gen. 24:14

- Jacob ‒ Ezek. 28:25; 37:25

- Moses ‒ Num. 12:7; Deut. 34:5

- Joshua ‒ Josh. 24:29 (after his death)

- David ‒ 2 Sam. 3:18; 7:5,8,26

verses.zh: 愿我的对头披戴羞辱！愿他们以自己的羞愧为外袍遮身！
verses.en: My accusers will be covered[NOTE:1] with shameand draped in humiliation as if it were a robe.
notes: The verbal sequence is perfect + prefixed form with vav (ו) consecutive. Since the psalmist seems to be anticipating the demise of his enemies, he may be using these forms rhetorically to describe the enemies’ defeat as if it were already accomplished. Some emend the text to קָמוּ יֵבֹשׁוּ (qamu yevoshu, “may those who attack me be humiliated”). See L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 75.

verses.zh: 我要用口极力称谢耶和华；我要在众人中间赞美他；
verses.en: I will thank the Lord profusely.[NOTE:1] In the middle of a crowd[NOTE:2] I will praise him,
notes: Heb “clothed.” Another option is to translate the prefixed verbal forms in this line and the next as jussives (“may my accusers be covered with shame”).
Heb “I will thank the Lord very much with my mouth.”
verses.commentary:
109:30-31 The psalmist praises YHWH for His faithfulness and justice.

- I will give thanks abundantly to the Lord ‒ BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense

- I will praise Him - BDB 237, KB 248, Piel IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense

Notice the different uses of the VOICE.

- the wicked, vv. 2-3,17,20

- the righteous, vv. 1,30

109:30 This reflects temple worship.

verses.zh: 因为他必站在穷乏人的右边，要救他脱离审判他灵魂的人。
verses.en: because he stands at the right hand of the needyto deliver him from those who threaten[NOTE:1] his life.
notes: Heb “many.”
verses.commentary:
109:31 "For He stands at the right hand of the needy" This is in direct contrast to the wicked accuser of Ps. 109:6.
This same phrase is used of Satan in Zech. 3:1.

YHWH is the defender of the needy, poor, socially outcast, and powerless!

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What does God's silence imply?

- List the actions of the wicked.

- Why do many commentators think the enemies were close friends?

- How does one explain the desire for violence against another person?

- How is Ps. 109:14 related to the concept of the book of life?
